speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the Government will look into deploying smaller and more discreet surveillance cameras for capturing high-rise littering so as to avoid alerting potential offenders to the deployment of these cameras.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask whether there is a timeframe in terms of reviewing the effectiveness of the current surveillance cameras?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I just did my home visits again and I still have the same feedback about the same debate that we had a few years ago, about how, when we put the surveillance camera there, it is good deterrence – people stopped littering or throwing out their cigarette butts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the minute we remove the cameras, they start again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, it is a cat-and-mouse game and it really is a waste of our current resources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can NEA look into this; look into deploying smaller, more discreet cameras so that we can have more effective enforcement on the ground?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are mindful of the feedback that we have gotten and indeed, we are aware of this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also need to consider other factors that will help us in apprehending the high-rise litter bugs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You will also need to make sure that the cameras are tamper-proof, not subjected to mischief, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And to mount it securely, you need a camera pole.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You need cameras with wider optical range because you usually do not have good enough information to know exactly which floor and, in fact, even which stack.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, you need a wider optical range from which to increase the chance to apprehend the high-rise littering offenders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is the reason why, if you look at it, it is not just the size of the camera, but the entire system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we will continue to look at developments in camera technology, including better image resolution and detection capabilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the end of the day, enforcement does act as a deterrent, but for a long-term sustainable solution, it must be that we want to encourage all Singapore residents to take collective responsibility, to encourage and influence each other to be civic-minded and to have positive social norms.
